Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going up, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves; going left, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves; going to number 8 would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order). So my guess (right from number 6) was wrong, so the line must go up.
Going up leaves no safe move afterwards; going left, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes right.

Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.

Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Going right would leave both cell (3,4) and cell (4,5) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going left would leave number 10 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes up.
The line must go right: left is number 12, which comes later.
Going up would cut off the top-right corner (2 cells). So the line goes around the edge to (4,1).
Cell (4,2) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
